source.text: וּבְכָל־זֹ֕את אֲנַ֛חְנוּ כֹּרְתִ֥ים אֲמָנָ֖ה וְכֹתְבִ֑ים וְעַל֙ הֶֽחָת֔וּם שָׂרֵ֥ינוּ לְוִיֵּ֖נוּ כֹּהֲנֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And in all this we [are] cutting a firm agreement and writing [it]; and on the sealed [document]: our princes, our Levites, our priests.

en.L: And because of all this we are making a firm agreement and writing [it]; and on the sealed [document are] our princes, our Levites, [and] our priests.
en.B: Because of all this, we are making a binding agreement and putting it in writing. On the sealed document are the names of our officials, our Levites and our priests.
en.R: Because of all this, we are making a firm agreement and putting it in writing. Our leaders, our Levites and our priests are putting their names and seals on it.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: in many Bibles this verse is 9:38
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text this verse opens chapter 10; many Bibles number it 9:38, the last verse of chapter 9, and so number the rest of this chapter (10:2-40 here) 10:1-39. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: in all this: because of all this, looking back to the prayer of chapter 9
decisions.reason: The phrase ties the pledge to the confession just made. The prayer ended with the people in great distress, serving foreign kings because of their sins (9:36-37); because of all this they now bind themselves to God's law. The words could also mean "in spite of all this", but the pledge reads most naturally as the people's answer to the prayer.

decisions.choice: cutting a firm agreement: making a binding pledge in writing
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for making a covenant ("cutting" a covenant), but the noun is not the usual word for covenant. It comes from the root for what is firm and reliable, and in 11:23 it means a fixed arrangement. The people bind themselves to keep the covenant God already made through Moses (verse 30); they are not making a new covenant with God.

decisions.choice: the sealed document: the written pledge, closed with the seals of those who confirmed it
decisions.reason: A document was confirmed by pressing seals into clay or wax, and those who sealed it stood as its guarantors and witnesses (compare Jeremiah 32:10-14). The names of those who sealed this one follow in verses 2-28.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's usual wording for this title of rank. Balanced and Readable add "the names of" or "putting their names and seals", which is what being "on the sealed document" means.

source.text: וְעַ֖ל הַחֲתוּמִ֑ים נְחֶמְיָ֧ה הַתִּרְשָׁ֛תָא בֶּן־חֲכַלְיָ֖ה וְצִדְקִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And on the sealed [documents]: Nehemiah the Tirshatha, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,

en.L: And on the sealed [documents were]: Nehemiah the Tirshatha, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
en.B: Those who sealed it were Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
en.R: These are the people who sealed it: Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,

decisions.choice: verse numbers: many Bibles begin chapter 10 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. Many Bibles count the verse before this one as 9:38 and begin chapter 10 here, so 10:2-40 here is 10:1-39 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the Tirshatha: a Persian title for the governor
decisions.reason: The word is a Persian title, used of the Persian-appointed governor of Judah (Ezra 2:63; Nehemiah 7:65, 69; 8:9). Nehemiah calls himself governor with the ordinary word as well (5:14). His name heads the list as the highest official.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah: a man named next to the governor, otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: Zedekiah stands between the governor and the priests, so he held some office close to Nehemiah, perhaps as his secretary or deputy. The text does not say what it was, and he is not named elsewhere in the book.

decisions.choice: the Tirshatha (Literal); the governor (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Persian title as a name; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as elsewhere in Ezra and Nehemiah.

decisions.choice: the priests who sealed: names that are often family names
decisions.reason: Many of the names in verses 3-9 appear again as the heads of priestly families in 12:1-7 and 12:12-21 (Seraiah, Jeremiah, Amariah, Malluch, Shebaniah, Harim, Meremoth, Ginnethon, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah, with small differences of spelling). So a name here may stand for a priestly family, sealed by the man who headed it at the time.

decisions.choice: Pashhur: a large priestly family among the returned exiles
decisions.reason: The descendants of Pashhur were one of the four priestly families that came back with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:38; Nehemiah 7:41), and some of them had married foreign wives (Ezra 10:22).

decisions.choice: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch: priestly names also found in chapter 12
decisions.reason: Hattush and Malluch are among the priests who came with Zerubbabel (12:2), and Shebaniah heads a priestly family in 12:14. See the note on verse 3.

decisions.choice: Harim, Meremoth: a priestly family and a priest who worked on the wall
decisions.reason: The descendants of Harim were a priestly family of the first return (Ezra 2:39; Nehemiah 7:42). A priest named Meremoth son of Uriah repaired two sections of the wall (3:4, 21), and a Meremoth heads a priestly family in 12:3.

decisions.choice: Daniel: a priest of the line of Ithamar, not the prophet
decisions.reason: A Daniel of the descendants of Ithamar came back with Ezra (Ezra 8:2). The prophet Daniel lived in Babylon a century earlier and was of the royal family, not a priest (Daniel 1:3-6).

decisions.choice: Abijah, Mijamin: names of priestly divisions
decisions.reason: Abijah and Mijamin are among the priestly families in 12:4-5 and 12:17, and both are names of the twenty-four divisions of priests in 1 Chronicles 24:9-10.

records.literal_gloss: Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah; these [were] the priests.

en.L: Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah; these [were] the priests.
en.B: Maaziah, Bilgai and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
en.R: Maaziah, Bilgai and Shemaiah. These were the priests.

decisions.choice: these were the priests: the close of the first group of names
decisions.reason: The words close the list of priests in verses 3-9, twenty-one names after Nehemiah and Zedekiah. The Levites (verses 10-14) and the leaders of the people (verses 15-28) follow, in the order of verse 1 reversed.

source.text: וְֽהַלְוִיִּ֑ם וְיֵשׁ֨וּעַ֙ בֶּן־אֲזַנְיָ֔ה בִּנּ֕וּי מִבְּנֵ֥י חֵנָדָ֖ד קַדְמִיאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And the Levites: and Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of [the] sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,

en.L: And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
en.B: The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the descendants of Henadad, Kadmiel,
en.R: These are the Levites who sealed it: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the family of Henadad, Kadmiel,

decisions.choice: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel: the leading Levites of the time
decisions.reason: The same three head the Levites who led the people's confession (9:4-5) and the Levites of the first return (12:8; Ezra 2:40). Men of the family of Henadad repaired parts of the wall (3:18, 24).

decisions.choice: These are the Levites who sealed it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the heading "and the Levites" introduces.

source.text: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֑ם שְׁבַנְיָ֧ה הֽוֹדִיָּ֛ה קְלִיטָ֖א פְּלָאיָ֥ה חָנָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,

en.L: and their brothers: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
en.B: and their fellow Levites: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
en.R: and their fellow Levites: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,

decisions.choice: their brothers: their fellow Levites
decisions.reason: As often in these lists, "brothers" means members of the same group or tribe, here the other Levites. Several of these names appear among the Levites who taught the law and led the prayer (8:7; 9:4-5).

decisions.choice: fellow Levites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the "brothers" are; Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: Hashabiah: a leading Levite
decisions.reason: A Levite named Hashabiah was ruler of half the district of Keilah and repaired part of the wall (3:17); a Hashabiah also came back with Ezra (Ezra 8:19, 24). The name was common, so they need not be the same man.

decisions.choice: Sherebiah; a second Shebaniah
decisions.reason: Sherebiah was one of the Levites who came with Ezra (Ezra 8:18) and helped teach the law (8:7). Shebaniah was already named in verse 11; two men may have had the same name, or the name may have been repeated in copying.

decisions.choice: the end of the Levites' names: seventeen in all
decisions.reason: The list of Levites (verses 10-14) has seventeen names. Hodiah appears in verse 11 as well, and Beninu only here. Some of these too may be family names.

source.text: רָאשֵׁ֖י הָעָ֑ם פַּרְעֹשׁ֙ פַּחַ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב עֵילָ֥ם זַתּ֖וּא בָּנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,

en.L: [The] heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
en.B: The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
en.R: These are the leaders of the people who sealed it: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,

decisions.choice: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani: the names of the great families of the return
decisions.reason: These names, and many in verses 16-28, are the family names of the list of returned exiles, in nearly the same order (7:8-15; Ezra 2:3-10). Each family's head probably sealed under the family's name. Pahath-Moab means "governor of Moab", a family name kept from some earlier office.

decisions.choice: heads (Literal); leaders (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Heads" is the word's picture; Balanced and Readable say "leaders". Readable repeats that these too sealed the agreement.

decisions.choice: Azgad, Bebai: families of the first return
decisions.reason: The descendants of Azgad and of Bebai are listed among the returned exiles (7:16-17; Ezra 2:11-12).

decisions.choice: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin: family names of the first return
decisions.reason: Bigvai and Adin are families in the list of returned exiles (7:19-20). Adonijah may be the same family called Adonikam there (7:18), whose name has the same first part.

decisions.choice: Ater, Hezekiah: perhaps one family named twice
decisions.reason: The list of returned exiles has "the descendants of Ater, of Hezekiah" as one family (7:21; Ezra 2:16). Here the two names stand apart, perhaps because each branch had its own head.

decisions.choice: Hashum, Bezai: families of the first return
decisions.reason: Both are families in the list of returned exiles (7:22-23). A Hodiah was also among the Levites in verses 11 and 14; this one is a lay leader.

decisions.choice: Nebai: the name as the Hebrew text is read
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell Nobai; the scribes' note in the margin gives the reading Nebai, which the vowels follow. The difference is one letter and does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: Hariph, Anathoth: a family and a town
decisions.reason: The descendants of Hariph are among the returned exiles (7:24). Anathoth is a priests' town north of Jerusalem (7:27; Jeremiah 1:1); here the name stands for the men from there.

decisions.choice: Meshullam: a common name
decisions.reason: Several men named Meshullam appear in Nehemiah: a builder of the wall (3:4, 30), a man who stood with Ezra (8:4), and a priest (verse 8 here). This one is among the lay leaders.

decisions.choice: Meshezabel, Zadok: names known from the building of the wall
decisions.reason: A Meshezabel was the grandfather of one of the builders (3:4), and a Zadok repaired a section (3:4, 29). The family may be the same; the text does not say.

decisions.choice: Anaiah: perhaps the man who stood beside Ezra
decisions.reason: An Anaiah stood at Ezra's right hand when he read the law (8:4).

decisions.choice: Hasshub: a builder of the wall
decisions.reason: A Hasshub repaired a section of the wall opposite his house (3:23); another, the son of Pahath-Moab, repaired another section (3:11).

decisions.choice: Hallohesh: a family whose head helped build the wall
decisions.reason: Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired a section of the wall with his daughters (3:12). The name begins with the Hebrew article, "the whisperer" or "the charmer".

decisions.choice: Rehum, Maaseiah: common names of the period
decisions.reason: Both names appear more than once in Ezra and Nehemiah (3:17, 23; 8:4); who these men were is not known.

decisions.choice: and: joining one more group of names
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "and" before Ahiah alone, in the middle of the list; it adds nothing to the sense.

decisions.choice: no "and" before Ahiah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the "and", as a list in the middle needs none; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: the end of the list: forty-four leaders of the people
decisions.reason: The leaders of the people (verses 15-28) number forty-four. With Nehemiah and Zedekiah, the twenty-one priests and the seventeen Levites, eighty-four names in all are on the sealed document. Malluch and Harim are also priestly names (verses 5-6); here they are lay families of the same name (Ezra 10:31-32).

source.text: וּשְׁאָ֣ר הָעָ֡ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַ֠לְוִיִּם הַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֨ים הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֜ים הַנְּתִינִ֗ים וְֽכָל־הַנִּבְדָּ֞ל מֵעַמֵּ֤י הָאֲרָצוֹת֙ אֶל־תּוֹרַ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים נְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם בְּנֵיהֶ֣ם וּבְנֹתֵיהֶ֑ם כֹּ֖ל יוֹדֵ֥עַ מֵבִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and every [one] separating himself from [the] peoples of the lands to [the] law of God, their wives, their sons and their daughters, every [one] knowing [and] understanding,

en.L: And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and everyone who had separated himself from the peoples of the lands to the law of God, their wives, their sons and their daughters, everyone who knew [and] understood,
en.B: The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to keep the law of God, together with their wives, their sons and their daughters, all who were old enough to understand,
en.R: The rest of the people joined in too: the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and everyone who had separated from the people living in the land in order to obey God's law, with their wives, sons and daughters, everyone old enough to understand.

decisions.choice: the rest of the people: the subject of a sentence that goes on into verse 30
decisions.reason: After the names of those who sealed, the whole community is listed, and the verb that tells what they did comes only at the start of verse 30: they hold fast to their leaders and take an oath. Verses 29-30 are one sentence.

decisions.choice: separated from the peoples of the lands to the law of God: turned away from the surrounding peoples' ways to keep God's law
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Israel keeping apart from foreign peoples and their worship (9:2; Ezra 6:21; 9:1). "To the law of God" says what they turned to. The phrase may include people of foreign birth who joined Israel's worship, as in Ezra 6:21, as well as Israelites who had mixed with the nations.

decisions.choice: everyone who knew and understood: everyone old enough to understand
decisions.reason: The same description is used of those who heard Ezra read the law (8:2-3): men, women, and children who could understand what was said. The pledge was taken by families, not by the leaders alone.

decisions.choice: the Nethinim (Literal), the temple servants (Balanced, Readable); the peoples of the lands (Literal, Balanced), the people living in the land (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's wording for these terms in Ezra and Nehemiah. Readable makes the sentence complete with "joined in too", which verse 30 states.

source.text: מַחֲזִיקִ֣ים עַל־אֲחֵיהֶם֮ אַדִּירֵיהֶם֒ וּבָאִ֞ים בְּאָלָ֣ה וּבִשְׁבוּעָ֗ה לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ בְּתוֹרַ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִתְּנָ֔ה בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֣ה עֶֽבֶד־הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְלִשְׁמ֣וֹר וְלַעֲשׂ֗וֹת אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֲדֹנֵ֔ינוּ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֖יו וְחֻקָּֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: holding fast to their brothers, their nobles, and entering into a curse and into an oath to walk in [the] law of God which was given by [the] hand of Moses, [the] slave of God, and to keep and to do all [the] commandments of YHWH our Lord, and his judgments and his statutes;

en.L: [are] holding fast to their brothers, their nobles, and entering into a curse and into an oath to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses the slave of God, and to keep and to do all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our Lord, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes,
en.B: join their fellow Israelites, their nobles, and bind themselves with a curse and an oath to walk in the law of God that was given through Moses the servant of God, and to keep and carry out all the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our Lord, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes.
en.R: They stood with their leaders and fellow Israelites. They swore an oath and called a curse down on themselves if they broke it. They promised to live by God's law, which God gave through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Moses, and to obey carefully all the commands, rules and laws of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our Lord.

decisions.choice: holding fast to their brothers, their nobles: joining their leaders in the pledge
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold firmly. The rest of the people take hold with the leading men who sealed the document, their own kinsmen, and commit themselves to the same pledge.

decisions.choice: entering into a curse and an oath: swearing an oath that calls down a curse on anyone who breaks it
decisions.reason: An oath in Israel often named the punishment that would fall on the one who broke it (compare 5:13, where Nehemiah shakes out his garment as a sign of the curse; Deuteronomy 29:11, 13, numbered 29:12, 14 in many Bibles). The covenant law itself sets out blessings and curses (Deuteronomy 28).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: A common Hebrew way of saying that God gave the law by means of Moses (8:14; 9:14).

decisions.choice: commandments, judgments and statutes: the whole of the law
decisions.reason: The three words name the law from different sides, as in Deuteronomy and in Nehemiah's prayer (1:7; 9:13-14). Together they mean everything the LORD commanded.

decisions.choice: slave of God (Literal); servant of God (Balanced); his servant (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's usual wording for "servant of the LORD/God" said of Moses. Readable says "which God gave through his servant Moses" to make plain who gave the law.

decisions.choice: commands, rules and laws
decisions.reason: Readable uses the project's plain words for these three terms and lists them together; the order of the Hebrew (commandments, judgments, statutes) is kept.

source.text: וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־נִתֵּ֥ן בְּנֹתֵ֖ינוּ לְעַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאֶת־בְּנֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א נִקַּ֖ח לְבָנֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and that we will not give our daughters to [the] peoples of the land, and their daughters we will not take for our sons;

en.L: and that we will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and their daughters we will not take for our sons;
en.B: We will not give our daughters in marriage to the peoples of the land or take their daughters as wives for our sons.
en.R: We will not let our daughters marry men from the people living in the land, and we will not let our sons marry their daughters.

decisions.choice: and that: the words of the oath begin, and the speakers become "we"
decisions.reason: The oath of verse 30 goes on with what was sworn, in the first person: "we will not ...". Verses 31-40 list the particular promises.

decisions.choice: no marriage with the peoples of the land: the law of Exodus 34:16 and Deuteronomy 7:3
decisions.reason: The law forbade marriage with the peoples of Canaan, because they would turn Israel's children to other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Ezra had faced the same problem (Ezra 9-10), and Nehemiah found it again later (13:23-27).

decisions.choice: in marriage; as wives
decisions.reason: Giving and taking daughters means marriage; Balanced and Readable say so. Balanced and Readable leave out "and that", which Literal keeps to show that the words continue the oath.

source.text: וְעַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֡רֶץ הַֽמְבִיאִים֩ אֶת־הַמַּקָּח֨וֹת וְכָל־שֶׁ֜בֶר בְּי֤וֹם הַשַּׁבָּת֙ לִמְכּ֔וֹר לֹא־נִקַּ֥ח מֵהֶ֛ם בַּשַּׁבָּ֖ת וּבְי֣וֹם קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְנִטֹּ֛שׁ אֶת־הַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖ית וּמַשָּׁ֥א כָל־יָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] peoples of the land who bring the wares and any grain on the day of the Sabbath to sell, we will not take from them on the Sabbath and on a holy day; and we will let go the seventh year and [the] debt of every hand;

en.L: and the peoples of the land who bring wares and any grain on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not take from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day; and we will let go the seventh year and [the] debt of every hand;
en.B: When the peoples of the land bring goods or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day. Every seventh year we will leave the land unworked and cancel every debt.
en.R: The people living in the land may bring goods or grain to sell on the Sabbath, but we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on any other holy day. Every seventh year we will let the land rest, and we will cancel all debts.

decisions.choice: buying on the Sabbath: trade with outsiders that broke the day of rest
decisions.reason: The law forbade work on the Sabbath (Exodus 20:8-10), and the prophets condemned trading on it (Amos 8:5; Jeremiah 17:21-22). Foreign traders did not keep the day, and buying from them was a way around it. Nehemiah later had to shut the gates against them (13:15-22).

decisions.choice: a holy day: the festival days on which no work was done
decisions.reason: Besides the weekly Sabbath, the law set apart days such as the first and last days of festivals as holy, with no ordinary work (Leviticus 23:7-8, 21, 35-36).

decisions.choice: let go the seventh year: leave the land unworked every seventh year
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Exodus 23:11, where the land is to be let go and left lying in the seventh year so the poor and the wild animals may eat from it. The people promise to keep that law.

decisions.choice: the debt of every hand: every loan, which is cancelled in the seventh year
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 15:1-2 commands that every creditor release what he has lent to his neighbor at the end of every seven years. The word for debt is the one used in 5:7, 10, where Nehemiah stopped the lending that was crushing the poor.

decisions.choice: buy (for "take")
decisions.reason: To take wares from the traders means to buy them; Balanced and Readable say so. Readable adds "other" before "holy day", since the Sabbath is one too.

source.text: וְהֶעֱמַ֤דְנוּ עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙ מִצְוֺ֔ת לָתֵ֥ת עָלֵ֛ינוּ שְׁלִשִׁ֥ית הַשֶּׁ֖קֶל בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And we established on ourselves commandments, to put on ourselves a third of the shekel in the year for [the] service of [the] house of our God,

en.L: And we laid on ourselves commandments, to charge ourselves a third of the shekel each year for the service of the house of our God,
en.B: We also took on ourselves the obligation to give {{units:about 1/8 ounce of silver|a third of a shekel}} each year for the service of the house of our God,
en.R: We also made a rule for ourselves: each year we will give {{units:about 1/8 ounce of silver|a third of a shekel}} to pay for the work of the temple of our God.

decisions.choice: commandments: obligations the people put on themselves
decisions.reason: The usual word for God's commandments is here used of duties the community laid on itself, which no law required in this form.

decisions.choice: a third of the shekel: a yearly temple tax
alternatives: half a shekel, as in Exodus 30:13
decisions.reason: Exodus 30:11-16 asked a half shekel from each man counted in the census, for the service of the tent of meeting. Here the yearly gift is a third of a shekel. Why it is smaller is not said: the people may have been poor, or the shekel used may have been heavier. Later, in the time of the New Testament, the tax was again a half shekel (Matthew 17:24).

decisions.choice: about 1/8 ounce of silver
decisions.reason: A shekel is about 2/5 ounce, so a third is a little over 1/8 ounce. A shekel was a weight of silver; Balanced and Readable say "of silver" so the modern measure makes sense, and the alternative keeps the original unit.

source.text: לְלֶ֣חֶם הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֡כֶת וּמִנְחַ֣ת הַתָּמִ֣יד וּלְעוֹלַ֣ת הַ֠תָּמִיד הַשַּׁבָּת֨וֹת הֶחֳדָשִׁ֜ים לַמּוֹעֲדִ֗ים וְלַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ וְלַ֣חַטָּא֔וֹת לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכֹ֖ל מְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית־אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: for [the] bread of the row and [the] grain offering of the continual and for [the] burnt offering of the continual, the Sabbaths, the new moons, for the appointed feasts and for the holy things and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all [the] work of [the] house of our God.

en.L: for the bread of the row and the continual grain offering and for the continual burnt offering, the Sabbaths, the new moons, for the appointed feasts and for the holy things and for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.
en.B: for the bread set out in rows, the regular grain offering and the regular burnt offering, the offerings for the Sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed feasts, the holy offerings, the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.
en.R: This will pay for the holy bread set out in rows, the grain offerings and burnt offerings made every day, the offerings for the Sabbaths, the new moon festivals and the other feasts, the holy offerings, and the sin offerings that make atonement for Israel. It will pay for all the work of the temple of our God.

decisions.choice: the bread of the row: the bread of the Presence, set out in rows each Sabbath
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were set in two rows on the table in the holy place each Sabbath (Leviticus 24:5-9); 1 Chronicles 9:32 uses the same name for it. Elsewhere it is called the bread of the Presence (Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: the continual offering: the burnt offering and grain offering made every morning and evening
decisions.reason: The word means "continual" and is the name for the daily offerings of Exodus 29:38-42 and Numbers 28:3-8, offered without a break.

decisions.choice: Sabbaths, new moons, appointed feasts, holy things, sin offerings: the offerings of the sacred calendar
decisions.reason: Numbers 28-29 lists the extra offerings for each Sabbath, the first day of each month, and the yearly feasts, including sin offerings. The "holy things" are probably the other offerings given to God. The people's tax was to pay for all of these.

decisions.choice: the bread of the row (Literal); the bread set out in rows (Balanced); the holy bread set out in rows (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "row" is; Readable adds "holy" so the reader knows this is not ordinary bread.

source.text: וְהַגּוֹרָל֨וֹת הִפַּ֜לְנוּ עַל־קֻרְבַּ֣ן הָעֵצִ֗ים הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים הַלְוִיִּם֮ וְהָעָם֒ לְ֠הָבִיא לְבֵ֨ית אֱלֹהֵ֧ינוּ לְבֵית־אֲבֹתֵ֛ינוּ לְעִתִּ֥ים מְזֻמָּנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֑ה לְבַעֵ֗ר עַל־מִזְבַּח֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ כַּכָּת֖וּב בַּתּוֹרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the lots we cast, the priests, the Levites and the people, for [the] offering of the wood, to bring [it] to [the] house of our God, by [the] house of our fathers, at times appointed year by year, to burn on [the] altar of YHWH our God, as [is] written in the law;

en.L: And we cast the lots, the priests, the Levites and the people, for the offering of the wood, to bring [it] to the house of our God by the house of our fathers, at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, as [it is] written in the law;
en.B: We, the priests, the Levites and the people, have cast lots for the wood offering, to decide which of our families is to bring wood to the house of our God at the set times each year, to burn on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, as it is written in the law.
en.R: We, the priests, the Levites and the people, have thrown lots to decide when each family must bring wood to the temple of our God. At set times every year they will bring wood to burn on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, as the law says.

decisions.choice: casting lots: leaving the choice to God
decisions.reason: Lots were drawn or thrown to settle questions fairly and to let the LORD decide (Proverbs 16:33). Lots also chose who would live in Jerusalem (11:1) and set the order of the priests' service (1 Chronicles 24:5).

decisions.choice: the wood offering: a supply of firewood for the altar, brought in turn by families
decisions.reason: The altar's fire was never to go out (Leviticus 6:5-6, numbered 6:12-13 in many Bibles), so wood was always needed. The law does not set a wood offering; "as it is written" refers to the burning on the altar that the law commands. Nehemiah mentions the wood offering again at the end of the book (13:31).

decisions.choice: by the house of our fathers: family by family
decisions.reason: The house of the fathers is the extended family, the unit in which the people were counted and organized. Each family took its turn.

decisions.choice: by the house of our fathers (Literal); which of our families (Balanced); each family (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's wording for the ancestral family. Balanced and Readable say what the lots decided, which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

source.text: וּלְהָבִ֞יא אֶת־בִּכּוּרֵ֣י אַדְמָתֵ֗נוּ וּבִכּוּרֵ֛י כָּל־פְּרִ֥י כָל־עֵ֖ץ שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֑ה לְבֵ֖ית יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and to bring [the] firstfruits of our ground and [the] firstfruits of all fruit of every tree year by year to [the] house of YHWH;

en.L: and to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree, year by year, to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}};
en.B: We will also bring the firstfruits of our soil and the firstfruits of all the fruit of every tree to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} each year.
en.R: Each year we will bring to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the first part of our crops and the first fruit from every tree.

decisions.choice: and to bring: another obligation the people took on
decisions.reason: The verb in this form ("to bring") continues the list of what the people bound themselves to do (verse 33). The same form goes on into verse 37.

decisions.choice: the firstfruits: the first of the harvest, given to the LORD
decisions.reason: The law commanded Israel to bring the first of its crops to the house of the LORD (Exodus 23:19; 34:26; Deuteronomy 26:1-11). They went to the priests for their food (Numbers 18:12-13).

decisions.choice: We will also bring
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make each promise its own sentence, with "we will"; Literal keeps the chain of "and to bring".

source.text: וְאֶת־בְּכֹר֤וֹת בָּנֵ֨ינוּ֙ וּבְהֶמְתֵּ֔ינוּ כַּכָּת֖וּב בַּתּוֹרָ֑ה וְאֶת־בְּכוֹרֵ֨י בְקָרֵ֜ינוּ וְצֹאנֵ֗ינוּ לְהָבִיא֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ לַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים הַמְשָׁרְתִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as [is] written in the law, and [the] firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to [the] house of our God, to the priests ministering in [the] house of our God;

en.L: and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as [it is] written in the law, and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God;
en.B: As it is written in the law, we will bring the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to the house of our God, to the priests who serve in the house of our God.
en.R: As the law says, we will bring our firstborn sons and the firstborn of our animals, our cattle, sheep and goats, to the priests who serve in the temple of our God.

decisions.choice: the firstborn of our sons: firstborn sons were given to God and bought back
decisions.reason: The law gives every firstborn to the LORD (Exodus 13:2, 12-13). Firstborn sons were not offered; they were redeemed by a payment to the priests, and so were unclean animals, while clean animals were sacrificed (Numbers 18:15-17). To bring the firstborn sons means to present them and pay their redemption.

decisions.choice: livestock; herds and flocks: animals in general, then cattle and sheep or goats
decisions.reason: The first word covers domestic animals in general; the second pair names the two kinds most often sacrificed, cattle and the smaller sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: our cattle, sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Readable names the animals the words for herds and flocks mean.

source.text: וְאֶת־רֵאשִׁ֣ית עֲרִיסֹתֵ֣ינוּ וּ֠תְרוּמֹתֵינוּ וּפְרִ֨י כָל־עֵ֜ץ תִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְיִצְהָ֗ר נָבִ֤יא לַכֹּהֲנִים֙ אֶל־לִשְׁכ֣וֹת בֵּית־אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ וּמַעְשַׂ֥ר אַדְמָתֵ֖נוּ לַלְוִיִּ֑ם וְהֵם֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַֽמְעַשְּׂרִ֔ים בְּכֹ֖ל עָרֵ֥י עֲבֹדָתֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] first of our dough and our contributions and [the] fruit of every tree, new wine and fresh oil, we will bring to the priests, to [the] storerooms of [the] house of our God; and [the] tithe of our ground to the Levites, and they, the Levites, [are] the ones receiving tithes in all [the] cities of our labor.

en.L: And the first of our dough and our contributions and the fruit of every tree, new wine and oil, we will bring to the priests, to the storerooms of the house of our God; and the tithe of our ground to the Levites, for they, the Levites, [are] the ones who collect the tithes in all the towns of our labor.
en.B: We will bring to the priests, to the storerooms of the house of our God, the first of our dough, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, the new wine and the olive oil; and we will bring the tithe of our crops to the Levites, for it is the Levites who collect the tithes in all the towns where we farm.
en.R: We will bring to the priests the first of our dough, our gifts, and the fruit of every tree, new wine and olive oil. We will bring them to the storerooms of the temple of our God. And we will give a tenth of our crops to the Levites, because the Levites collect the tenth in all the towns where we work the land.

decisions.choice: the first of our dough: the first loaf of each baking, given to the priests
decisions.reason: Numbers 15:20-21 commands Israel to give the first of its dough as a contribution to the LORD, and Ezekiel 44:30 says it goes to the priests.

decisions.choice: the tithe to the Levites: a tenth of the harvest, the Levites' living
decisions.reason: The Levites had no land of their own and lived on the tithes of the people's crops (Numbers 18:21-24). Verse 39 adds what the Levites must give in turn.

decisions.choice: the towns of our labor: the towns where the people farm
decisions.reason: The word for labor is often used of farm work (Exodus 1:14; Psalm 104:23). The Levites went out to collect the tithe where it was grown, rather than waiting for it to be brought.

decisions.choice: olive oil; our crops
decisions.reason: The oil is fresh olive oil, and "the tithe of our ground" is a tithe of what the ground produces. Readable says "gifts" for contributions and "a tenth" for tithe, in plainer words.

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֧ן בֶּֽן־אַהֲרֹ֛ן עִם־הַלְוִיִּ֖ם בַּעְשֵׂ֣ר הַלְוִיִּ֑ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם יַעֲל֨וּ אֶת־מַעֲשַׂ֤ר הַֽמַּעֲשֵׂר֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ אֶל־הַלְּשָׁכ֖וֹת לְבֵ֥ית הָאוֹצָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the priest, [the] son of Aaron, will be with the Levites in the tithing of the Levites, and the Levites will bring up the tithe of the tithe to [the] house of our God, to the storerooms of the house of the treasure;

en.L: And the priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites collect tithes, and the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasure house;
en.B: A priest descended from Aaron is to be with the Levites when they collect the tithes, and the Levites are to bring a tenth of the tithes up to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.
en.R: A priest from Aaron's family will go with the Levites when they collect the tenth. Then the Levites will take a tenth of what they receive up to the temple of our God and put it in the storerooms of the treasury.

decisions.choice: the priest, the son of Aaron: a priest of Aaron's line, not one named man
decisions.reason: The article points to whichever priest is on duty. "Son of Aaron" means descendant of Aaron, the family to which the priesthood belonged. His presence made sure the priests' share was set aside.

decisions.choice: the tithe of the tithe: the tenth the Levites themselves give to the priests
decisions.reason: Numbers 18:26-28 commands the Levites to give a tenth of the tithes they receive as the LORD's contribution, for Aaron the priest.

decisions.choice: bring up; storerooms of the treasure house (Literal), of the treasury (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Bring up" keeps the Hebrew picture of going up to Jerusalem and the temple. "Storerooms" is used for the same word through these chapters.

source.text: כִּ֣י אֶל־הַ֠לְּשָׁכוֹת יָבִ֨יאוּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וּבְנֵ֣י הַלֵּוִ֗י אֶת־תְּרוּמַ֣ת הַדָּגָן֮ הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָר֒ וְשָׁם֙ כְּלֵ֣י הַמִּקְדָּ֔שׁ וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ הַמְשָׁ֣רְתִ֔ים וְהַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֖ים וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א נַעֲזֹ֖ב אֶת־בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For to the storerooms will bring [the] sons of Israel and [the] sons of Levi the contribution of the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, and there [are the] vessels of the sanctuary and the priests ministering and the gatekeepers and the singers; and we will not forsake [the] house of our God.

en.L: For to the storerooms the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and the sons of Levi shall bring the contribution of the grain, the new wine and the oil, and there [are] the vessels of the sanctuary and the priests who minister and the gatekeepers and the singers; and we will not forsake the house of our God.
en.B: For the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the Levites are to bring the contributions of grain, new wine and olive oil to the storerooms, where the vessels of the sanctuary are kept and where the priests who serve, the gatekeepers and the singers are. We will not neglect the house of our God.
en.R: The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the Levites must bring their gifts of grain, new wine and olive oil to these storerooms. The things used in the temple are kept there, and the priests on duty, the gatekeepers and the singers stay there. We will not neglect the temple of our God.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the gifts go to the storerooms
decisions.reason: The verse explains verses 38-39: the storerooms are where the temple's vessels and its servants are, so that is where their food must be brought.

decisions.choice: we will not forsake the house of our God: the pledge Nehemiah later had to enforce
decisions.reason: The last promise sums up the rest. When Nehemiah returned later he found that the Levites' portions had not been given, and he asked, "Why is the house of God forsaken?", using the same verb (13:10-11).

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel and the sons of Levi: the lay people and the Levites
decisions.reason: The sons of Israel here are the people as distinct from the Levites; the sons of Levi are the Levites, who bring the tithe of the tithe (verse 39).

decisions.choice: neglect (for "forsake")
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or abandon. Here it means to fail to support the temple, so Balanced and Readable say "neglect"; Literal keeps "forsake".
